public_rationale: The forecast has no deadline. The records show federal policy choices and a state investigation, but neither establishes the prevailing relationship between companies and government across AI rulemaking. The investigation qualifies an absolute reading of government acquiescence; Marcus's wording about the default does not require that absolute reading. No decisive event meeting the early-resolution rule was established.
limitations: The evidence is not a census of US AI regulation or industry lobbying.
State enforcement and federal rulemaking are different activities.
Policy agreement does not by itself prove capture.

our_interpretation: The surrounding discussion makes US AI regulation the principal scope, although the wording also refers to governments generally.
The ordinary reading predicts a prevailing pattern of company control over substantive regulatory choices. It does not assert that governments will never oppose any company.
By default describes the predicted tendency, rather than a separate conditional antecedent.
No deadline, company roster, or measure of regulatory control is supplied.
criteria.support_condition: A completed regulatory settlement, supported by records of company proposals and government decisions, establishes that major AI companies determined the substantive rules and governments accepted their limits.
criteria.contradiction_condition: A completed regulatory settlement establishes substantive government control over the principal rules despite documented opposition from major AI companies. An isolated disagreement is insufficient to refute a prediction about the default pattern.
